name: @lovrabet/dataset-mcp-server

tools.name: login
tools.description: Login to Lovrabet to authenticate for dataset queries.

env.description: Environment (optional, uses LOVRABET_ENV or defaults to online)

tools.name: list_datasets
tools.description: Get list of all datasets with metadata and table relations (ER Config). Use includeRelations: false for faster response.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

tools.name: search_datasets
tools.description: Search datasets by keyword (searches in name, table name, code, and description).

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

tools.name: get_dataset_detail
tools.description: Get detailed dataset information including fields, operations, and bidirectional relations (outgoing + incoming). Returns _relations (structured graph edges), _relationsSummary (natural language overview), and _usageHints (actionable advice based on the dataset's position in the relation graph).

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

includeRelations.description: Include bidirectional relations, summary, and usage hints (default: true)

tools.name: get_dataset_operations
tools.description: Get list of all API operations for a dataset. Prefer "filter" for queries, "getOne" for single record by ID.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

tools.name: get_operation_detail
tools.description: Get detailed operation information including request/response examples.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

operationName.description: Operation name (e.g., filter, getOne, create, update)

tools.name: generate_sdk_code
tools.description: Generate TypeScript SDK code for a dataset operation, including field metadata. Check user's @lovrabet/sdk version in package.json first.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

operationName.description: Operation name (e.g., filter, getOne, create, update)

useAlias.description: Use camelCase alias instead of dataset_[code] pattern (default: false)

tools.name: list_sql_queries
tools.description: List all available custom SQL queries with metadata and parameters.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

tools.name: execute_custom_sql
tools.description: Execute a custom SQL query by sqlCode. Get sqlCode from list_sql_queries first.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

tools.name: generate_sql_code
tools.description: Generate code for a custom SQL query. Validates sqlCode exists first. Use target to switch between Frontend SDK and Backend Function code patterns.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

target.description: Target context: "sdk" (Frontend SDK, default) or "bff" (Backend Function). SDK returns {execSuccess, execResult} wrapper; BFF returns rows directly.

tools.name: validate_sql_content
tools.description: Validate SQL content without saving. Detects SQL type (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/DDL) and validates table/column existence. Supports MyBatis syntax.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

tools.name: save_or_update_custom_sql
tools.description: Save or update a custom SQL query via toolbox. SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / WITH are auto-saved; DELETE and DDL are blocked — write a local draft file and tell the user to operate manually. If blocked=true (last submitter conflict), do NOT retry. On success, also write a local copy to src/custom_sql/<sqlName>.sql. Supports MyBatis syntax. Get dbId from get_dataset_detail.

appCode.description: Application code (optional if LOVRABET_APP_CODE env var is set)

cookie.description: Authentication cookie (optional, uses stored cookie from login if not provided)

sqlName.description: SQL name/label (optional; MCP auto-extracts from @lovrabet.sqlName comment, or toolbox generates fallback)

sqlCode.description: Known sqlCode — use to directly target the record for update, skipping name lookup

dbId.description: Database ID from get_dataset_detail — required when creating new SQL, optional when updating

sqlContent.description: SQL content (SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/WITH auto-saved; DELETE/DDL blocked). Supports MyBatis syntax.

id.description: SQL ID (kept for backward compatibility, not used by toolbox)

instructions:
You are an AI assistant helping developers work with the Lovrabet data platform.

## Two Runtime Contexts: Frontend SDK vs Backend Function (BFF)

Lovrabet has two code execution contexts with **identical calling methods but different return structures**:

### Frontend TypeScript SDK (`@lovrabet/sdk`)
- Runs in browser/Node.js, imported via `import { LovrabetClient } from '@lovrabet/sdk'`
- Model operations return unwrapped data on success, throw LovrabetError on error
- SQL execution returns wrapper: `{ execSuccess, execResult }`

### Backend Function (BFF)
- Runs on Lovrabet server, function signature: `export default async function(params, context) { ... }`
- Use `context.client` to access the same SDK methods
- Model operations behave the same as SDK
- **SQL execution returns direct array** `T[]`, errors throw exceptions (no wrapper)

> **CRITICAL**: Always ask or determine which context the user is working in before generating code.

## SDK Usage Patterns

### Model Access (SDK >= 1.2.0)
- Default: `client.models.dataset_[code].filter()`
- Alias: `client.models.[alias].filter()` (check user's createClient/registerModels config for actual alias)
- For SDK < 1.2.0: only `client.models.[key]` where key is defined in createClient/registerModels

### SDK Return Value Behavior
- **On Success**: Returns ONLY the 'data' field content (e.g., `{ id: 123, name: "..." }`)
- **On Error**: Throws LovrabetError with `{ message, status, code, data }`
- **Always use try-catch** when calling SDK methods

### Data Query Best Practices
- **filter**: Most flexible, supports complex WHERE conditions, pagination, sorting — use this for queries
- **getOne**: Single record by primary key ID only
- **getList**: Simple unfiltered listing (rarely needed)

## Custom SQL Execution

### Frontend SDK
```typescript
const data = await client.sql.execute({ sqlCode: 'xxx', params: { key: 'value' } });
if (!data.execSuccess) throw new Error('SQL execution failed');
const results = data.execResult || [];
```

### Backend Function (BFF)
```javascript
// context.client.sql.execute returns rows directly — NO wrapper object
const rows = await context.client.sql.execute({ sqlCode: 'xxx', params: { key: 'value' } });
// rows is T[] directly, errors throw exceptions
```

> Note: `client.api.executeSql()` is deprecated. Use `client.sql.execute()`.

## MyBatis Dynamic SQL
SQL content supports MyBatis syntax: `#{param}`, `<if test="">`, `<where>`, `<foreach>`.
Use `< > &` for < > & in SQL content (not in `<if test="">` attributes).

## Workflow Tips
- Use list_datasets to discover available datasets
- Use get_dataset_detail to see fields, operations, and database info (dbId)
- Use generate_sdk_code to get ready-to-use TypeScript code
- Use list_sql_queries to find existing custom SQLs before creating new ones
- validate_sql_content before save_or_update_custom_sql
- save_or_update_custom_sql routes through toolbox; DELETE/DDL are blocked; if blocked=true (last submitter conflict) tell the user to operate manually, do NOT retry; after a successful save also write a local copy to src/custom_sql/<sqlName>.sql
- generate_sql_code supports target='sdk' (default) or target='bff' for context-appropriate code
